candidates.basis: NL3; source tr_0001 has no event; closed transition line 25 is the root initial edge and has no trigger; target is HumanDrivingMode.
candidates.expected: On power on, the system's owner-local initial edge enters HumanDrivingMode.
candidates.observed: The root initial edge enters HumanDrivingMode but carries no power-on trigger.
candidates.reason: The required root entry target exists, but the closed model's root initial edge has no power-on trigger. Because the atomic contract is initial_entry and the required owner-local edge reaches the target, this is a semantic gap in the stated startup condition rather than a missing endpoint.
candidates.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: Initial pseudostate edges may be implicitly activated at machine startup, so the absence of an explicit event may be intentional; the supplied contract nevertheless explicitly names power on.
candidates.title: Root Initial Entry Is Not Power-On Specific

candidates.basis: NL4 endpoint and guard hint; source tr_0002; closed transition line 26 reaches AutonomousMode with trigger front_distance_10 and guard null; event consumer is reachable.
candidates.expected: HumanDrivingMode transitions to AutonomousMode under guard front_distance > 10.
candidates.observed: The endpoint exists and is reachable, and front_distance_10 is the trigger, but the transition guard is null.
candidates.reason: The exact HumanDrivingMode-to-AutonomousMode endpoint exists and is reachable, but its closed transition has no parsed guard. The contract independently requires front_distance > 10, so the endpoint success does not discharge the guard-bearing behavioral requirement.
candidates.requirement_quote: when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The FCSTM event name front_distance_10 may encode the threshold as an event-level condition; the supplied model facts do not establish that event identity is semantically equivalent to the required guard.
candidates.title: Autonomous Endpoint Has No Required Guard

candidates.basis: NL4.2; source tr_0007 directly targets HumanDrivingMode; closed transition line 16 targets [*] and emits R45RouteToken = 7; outer line 23 targets HumanDrivingMode only under the route-token guard; event consumer is reachable on line 16.
candidates.expected: AutoFinalState transitions to HumanDrivingMode on human steering cmd with brake pressed.
candidates.observed: AutoFinalState emits the same event while transitioning to the enclosing exit; a separate outer transition reaches HumanDrivingMode only when R45RouteToken == 7.
candidates.reason: The exact AutoFinalState source and HumanDrivingMode target concepts are bound, but the selected closed transition from AutoFinalState goes to the composite exit pseudo-state. The outer guarded transitions route only on compiler-owned R45RouteToken values, so no direct closed transition realizes the required event-and-brake endpoint.
candidates.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The protected compiler-generated exit routing may be the intended realization of the authored transition, but the supplied working-contract macro closure does not establish direct endpoint equivalence for the required event-and-guard relation.
candidates.title: Auto Final Returns Through Exit Routing

candidates.reason: The required AutonomousMode-to-final-state endpoint is realized by the exact closed transition line 24, and the Power_Off consumer is reachable. No endpoint issue is emitted for this contract.

candidates.basis: NL5 termination obligation; active descendant transition inventory lines 13-19; AutoFinalState line 16 returns through the composite exit route; root final target is represented by [*].
candidates.expected: AutonomousMode must terminate by reaching final state without continued autonomous-mode behavior.
candidates.observed: AutonomousMode reaches its final exit on Power_Off, but active descendants retain alternate event-driven exits and AutoFinalState can route back to HumanDrivingMode.
candidates.reason: Although AutonomousMode has an exact Power_Off exit transition to the root final pseudo-state, its active descendants also have Power_Off exits and event-driven routes, and AutoFinalState can return to HumanDrivingMode.
